items.title: CVE-2026-85046: Google Google Chromium V8 Type Confusion Vulnerability
items.one_liner: An actively exploited Chromium V8 flaw requires urgent patching across all Chrome, Edge, and Opera browser deployments.
items.summary: CISA has added a critical Chromium V8 type confusion vulnerability, designated CVE-2026-85046, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue. The flaw allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code within the browser sandbox via a specially crafted HTML page. It impacts major Chromium-based browsers, including Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera. Federal agencies and enterprise defenders are mandated to apply vendor mitigations or discontinue product use by September 18, 2026.
key_facts: Affected products: Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Opera
items.bottom_line: Apply vendor updates immediately across Chromium-based browsers to prevent remote code execution attacks.

items.title: Update on Attacks by Threat Group APT-C-60 in 2026
items.one_liner: APT-C-60 abuses developer platforms and Git execution to deploy SpyGlace malware.
items.summary: JPCERT/CC updated its analysis on threat group APT-C-60, detailing campaigns in 2026 that use spear-phishing emails containing Proton Drive links or direct attachments to deliver malicious RAR archives. The extraction drops an LNK file that leverages mshta.exe to run obfuscated JavaScript, downloads contributing[1].txt via jsDelivr, and uses git.exe to execute component scripts. The threat actor abuses developer services and CDNs including GitLab, jsDelivr, Codeberg, and GitHub as infrastructure to deploy SpyGlace malware versions v3.1.15 to v3.1.18.
key_facts: Services Abused: GitLab, jsDelivr, Codeberg, GitHub
items.bottom_line: Defenders cannot rely on communication destination allowlists for developer platforms like GitLab and GitHub, as APT groups routinely weaponize them.

claims.text: In the case we observed, the spear-phishing email contained a Proton Drive link, which was used to lure the victim into downloading a RAR file from Proton Drive.

items.title: Broadcom Patches Critical VMware Workstation and Fusion VM-Escape Vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: VMware users on Windows, Linux, and macOS must update to 26H1u1 immediately to prevent guest-to-host VM escapes.
items.summary: Broadcom has released security advisory VMSA-2026-0007 to address two critical vulnerabilities in VMware Workstation and Fusion. The first, CVE-2026-59346 (CVSS 9.3), is an integer overflow in the VMXNET3 virtual network adapter that allows host-level code execution from a guest VM. The second, CVE-2026-59347 (CVSS 8.1), is a stack-based buffer overflow in the Host-Guest File System (HGFS) component. Both vulnerabilities affect versions 25H2 and 26H1 and have been patched in version 26H1u1.
key_facts: CVE-2026-59347: CVSS 8.1, HGFS stack-based buffer overflow
items.bottom_line: These vulnerabilities allow an attacker with local admin privileges on a guest VM to execute code on the host, effectively breaking the isolation boundary of the virtualization platform.

items.title: CVE-2026-75754 (CRITICAL 10.0): Missing Authentication for Critical Function, Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), and Use of Hard-coded Crede…
items.one_liner: A CVSS 10.0 chain in ASUS Control Center grants unauthenticated attackers full root access and control over enterprise endpoints.
items.summary: A critical maximum-severity vulnerability (CVSS 10.0) tracked as CVE-2026-75754 has been disclosed in ASUS Control Center. The issue combines missing authentication, server-side request forgery (SSRF), and hardcoded credentials. An unauthenticated remote attacker can extract an encryption key via HTTP, trigger local SSH activation on port 2222, and log in with hardcoded root credentials to gain total remote control over managed workstations, servers, and PCs.
key_facts: Attack mechanism: Missing auth, SSRF, hardcoded credentials
items.bottom_line: Patch ASUS Control Center immediately to prevent complete network takeover via hardcoded credentials and SSRF.

claims.text: The vulnerability carries a maximum CVSS base score of 10.0 (CRITICAL).
claims.support_span: CVSS base score 10.0 (CRITICAL).

claims.support_span: Missing Authentication for Critical Function, Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), and Use of Hard-coded Credentials in ASUS Control Center allow an unauthorized user to obtain the encryption key via an HTTP request, causing a local service to enable SSH on port 2222. The attacker can then log in with the hardcode credentials to obtain a root shell, enabling direct reading, writing, and deletion of data on ASUS Control Center, as well as remote control of all servers, PCs, and workstations within the company.

items.title: You’re Back In The Room (Citrix NetScaler Pre-Auth RCE CVE-2026-8452(?))
items.one_liner: watchTowr Labs analyzes a critical heap overflow vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler SAML configurations.
items.summary: Security researchers at watchTowr Labs have published an analysis of a heap overflow vulnerability patched in recent Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway security bulletins, which they believe corresponds to CVE-2026-8452. The vulnerability is reachable when NetScaler appliances are configured to use SAML as either a Service Provider or an Identity Provider. Affected versions include NetScaler ADC and Gateway 14.1 before 14.1-72.61 and 13.1 before 13.1-63.18. The researchers discuss the mechanics of the heap corruption issue and its potential to achieve remote code execution on widely deployed enterprise edge appliances.

Vector: SAML configured as SP or IdP
items.bottom_line: Citrix NetScaler appliances configured for SAML are vulnerable to a pre-auth heap overflow leading to potential RCE if unpatched.

items.title: Repeat-After-Me: Black-Box Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection
items.one_liner: A new visual prompt injection technique can compromise AI agents via images, bypassing text-based defenses to trigger RCE and data theft.
items.summary: Researchers have developed 'Repeat-After-Me,' a black-box visual prompt injection attack that forces Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to perform unauthorized actions or leak sensitive information. Unlike text-based injections, this method uses minimally injected images that do not require the user to verbally authorize the task. The attack achieved success rates exceeding 80% on Qwen3.6-27B and 47% on GPT-5.5, demonstrating the ability to trigger remote code execution and data exfiltration in real-world agent deployments like OpenClaw.
items.bottom_line: AI agents that process untrusted images are vulnerable to silent, high-success prompt injections that can execute arbitrary code without user consent.

items.one_liner: CSF firewall versions below 16.31 contain a critical RCE vulnerability via an insecure Apache CGI mapping.
items.summary: An insecure Apache configuration vulnerability exists in ConfigServer Security & Firewall (CSF) versions prior to 16.31, affecting installations with CSF Messenger v3 and HTTPS mode enabled. The flaw improperly maps /usr/bin as CGI programs through the Messenger v3 HTTPS virtual host. This allows an unauthenticated remote attacker whose IP address is blocked to request a mapped executable and execute arbitrary commands with Apache user privileges. WebPros addressed this critical issue in version 16.31.

items.title: AWSHound: An OpenSource AWS OpenGraph Collector
items.one_liner: AWSHound is a new open-source BloodHound collector that maps multi-hop AWS IAM attack paths using offline policy evaluation.
items.summary: SpecterOps has introduced AWSHound, a read-only OpenSource tool designed to map complex, multi-hop IAM permission paths across AWS accounts and organizations into BloodHound Community Edition (BHCE) OpenGraph datasets. Unlike standard single-action AWS evaluations, AWSHound performs an offline identity access management policy evaluation—factoring in SCPs, RCPs, permissions boundaries, and resource policies—to construct genuine, actionable attack paths that resolve to Allow. This helps defenders identify privilege escalation vectors that span multiple identities and services before attackers exploit them.
key_facts: Platform compatibility: BloodHound Community Edition (BHCE) and Enterprise Edition
items.bottom_line: Cloud defenders can use AWSHound to uncover hidden, multi-hop IAM privilege escalation paths across complex AWS Organizations that standard policy checks miss.

claims.support_span: Before it draws a single edge, it runs an offline identity access management (IAM) policy evaluation, such that an edge only exists when a principal’s effective permissions actually resolve to Allow once SCPs, RCPs, and permissions boundaries have all had their say.

items.title: Telerik UI Padding-Oracle Bug Chained to Unauthenticated RCE — Public Exploit Released
items.one_liner: Public exploit tooling combines an AES-CBC padding oracle and type resolution flaws in Telerik UI to achieve unauthenticated RCE.
items.summary: Security firm TantoSec published a public exploit chain and command-line tool targeting vulnerabilities in Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution. Progress Software patched the underlying issues in version 2026.2.708 on July 8. Exploitation requires specific non-default configurations, including a rendered RadAsyncUpload control and an explicit application encryption key. The vulnerability leverages an AES-CBC padding oracle (CVE-2026-13182) to forge encrypted upload configurations and bypass type-resolution restrictions (CVE-2026-13181), allowing attackers to deserialize a gadget and load a mixed-mode DLL payload.
items.bottom_line: TantoSec has released public exploit tooling for patched Telerik UI vulnerabilities, enabling unauthenticated RCE on misconfigured servers.

items.one_liner: Attackers are using rogue ScreenConnect installations to deploy a multi-stage VBScript chain for system compromise.
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a worm-like campaign abusing ConnectWise ScreenConnect to deploy a four-stage VBScript chain on compromised systems. These clients then execute a series of scripts that profile the host, check for security software, and download secondary payloads, including PowerShell scripts for further exploitation.

items.title: Multiple Class Action Lawsuits Filed Against IDScan
items.one_liner: IDScan.net faces multiple class-action lawsuits following a mega-breach exposing millions of driver's licenses and identity records.
items.summary: At least four class-action lawsuits have been filed against IDScan.net in the US District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana following reports of a massive driver's license data breach. A Russian cybercrime forum post advertised a service called "Nexus" containing over 153 million driver's licenses and 10 million other ID documents before the forum was taken down. IDScan.net provides B2B identification verification services for high-profile enterprises including Hertz, FedEx, and numerous cannabis dispensaries, raising calls from security experts to regulate large data broker holdings similarly to protected health information.

items.title: Your MikroTik Router May Already Be Compromised: Look for SSH User “-2”
items.one_liner: MikroTrick zero-day chain (CVE-2026-67276 / CVE-2026-86060) is actively hijacking internet-facing MikroTik routers via SSH.
items.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting an unauthenticated zero-day attack chain dubbed MikroTrick against internet-facing MikroTik RouterOS devices. items.title: Rhysida Publishes Berlin Government Data After €2m Extortion Demand Refused
items.one_liner: A massive 5.7 TB data breach of Berlin government systems by Rhysida highlights the risks of ransomware leaks targeting public infrastructure.
items.summary: Berlin’s state government confirmed that the Rhysida ransomware gang published a stolen 5.7 TB dataset on the dark web after the government refused a 30 bitcoin extortion demand worth approximately €2m. The published leak includes around 1.4 million files, featuring sensitive state emergency disaster plans regarding CBRN threats as well as personal data and payroll files belonging to state employees. The State of Berlin stated it will not give in to extortion, while forensic experts continue to analyze the leaked files to notify affected individuals on a risk-based basis.
items.bottom_line: Berlin's refusal to pay a €2m Rhysida ransom resulted in the public leak of 5.7 TB of government files, including sensitive CBRN emergency plans.

items.title: New Ted Backdoor Hides Inside Victims' Own HAProxy Builds to Intercept Web Traffic
items.one_liner: A stealthy Linux implant hides inside trojanized HAProxy builds to intercept traffic and evade detection by manipulating connection counters.
items.summary: A sophisticated Linux toolkit named 'ted' has been discovered embedded within trojanized HAProxy binaries at two South Korean organizations. The implant intercepts web traffic, serves altered content, and hides its command-and-control (C2) activity by manipulating HAProxy's internal connection counters. The toolkit also includes a trojanized SSH daemon and other system binaries to maintain persistence and capture credentials. Rapid7 attributes the activity with medium confidence to North Korean state-sponsored actors.

items.bottom_line: Attackers are deploying trojanized HAProxy binaries that intercept traffic and erase C2 activity from system logs and connection counters.

items.one_liner: A critical CVSS 9.8 LFI flaw in the Divi Ajax Filter WordPress plugin allows unauthenticated arbitrary PHP execution.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-11613) has been identified in the Divi Ajax Filter plugin for WordPress, affecting all versions up to and including 5.1.2. The flaw arises in the 'custom_loop_template' parameter when 'loop_templates' is set to 'custom-template', enabling Local File Inclusion. Unauthenticated remote attackers can leverage this to include and execute arbitrary PHP files on the server. This allows threat actors to bypass access controls, expose sensitive data, or achieve remote code execution if file upload paths are accessible.
key_facts: Affected software: Divi Ajax Filter for WordPress <= 5.1.2
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can achieve PHP code execution via an LFI vulnerability in Divi Ajax Filter <= 5.1.2.

claims.text: Divi Ajax Filter versions up to 5.1.2 allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary PHP files.
claims.support_span: This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files.

claims.text: The vulnerability relies on the loop_templates parameter being set to custom-template.
claims.support_span: This vulnerability is only exploitable when the loop_templates parameter is set to 'custom-template'.

items.title: Chaotic Eclipse Released A PoC For NVIDIA GreenSection Memory Corruption Zero-Day
items.one_liner: Researcher Chaotic Eclipse released PoCs for zero-days in NVIDIA Windows components, Kaspersky, Avast, and CrowdStrike Falcon.
items.summary: Security researcher Chaotic Eclipse has published a proof-of-concept for a zero-day memory corruption vulnerability in NVIDIA Windows user-mode components, dubbed GreenSection. The flaw stems from a global memory section with universal read/write access that reuses data at runtime, triggering an out-of-bounds memory write that can cross user boundaries or compromise dwm.exe. The disclosure follows a series of recent zero-days released by the same researcher targeting endpoint defense tools, including Kaspersky Endpoint Security (HardBreacher), Avast Antivirus (PrettyPrague), and CrowdStrike Falcon (FalconFlank).
key_facts: NVIDIA Exploit: GreenSection (Memory corruption / Out-of-bounds write)
Security product exploits: HardBreacher (Kaspersky), PrettyPrague (Avast), FalconFlank (CrowdStrike)
items.bottom_line: A newly released PoC exposes an out-of-bounds write zero-day in NVIDIA user-mode components alongside several antivirus zero-days.

claims.text: NVIDIA Windows user-mode components expose a globally writable memory section leading to an out-of-bounds write.
claims.support_span: Several NVIDIA components share a global memory section that gives all users full read/write access. Although the software performs checks to prevent misuse, it reuses data from this shared memory at runtime, which can lead to an out-of-bounds memory write.

claims.text: Chaotic Eclipse also released zero-day exploits targeting Kaspersky, Avast, and CrowdStrike Falcon.
claims.support_span: Recently, Chaotic Eclipse released exploits targeting other anti-malware and defense solutions.

items.title: Berlin investigates new data leak after hackers publish stolen login credentials
items.one_liner: Berlin authorities investigate a government data leak after hackers publish stolen employee and resident login credentials.
items.summary: German authorities are investigating a data leak after hackers published login credentials and files stolen from Berlin's government network over the weekend. The incident follows a cyberattack discovered in mid-August compromising two ministries responsible for urban development and transport. The leaked information includes names, addresses, bank details, and correspondence belonging to public employees and residents. The Rhysida ransomware group claimed responsibility for the breach in late August, alleging they stole 5.79 terabytes of data, though Berlin officials have refused to pay ransom demands and disconnected affected systems.
key_facts: Affected departments: Ministry for Urban Development and Housing; Ministry for Transport, Mobility, Climate Protection and the Environment
items.bottom_line: Hackers have published stolen login credentials from a Berlin government network breach, prompting ongoing investigations and refusal of ransom demands.

items.one_liner: IDScan faces lawsuits and an FBI probe after 153 million driver's licenses were leaked on the dark web.
items.summary: Identity verification provider IDScan faces multiple class-action lawsuits and an FBI investigation following allegations that over 153 million driver's licenses were breached and offered on dark-web service Nexus. items.one_liner: An AI agent using Claude Opus successfully reverse-engineered an n-day patch into an RCE exploit chain for Papercut NG in 90 minutes.
items.summary: Using Claude Opus within a secure harness, a security researcher prompted the AI agent to reverse-engineer a patch for an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability in Papercut NG. items.bottom_line: Advanced LLMs can rapidly convert software patches into functional exploit chains, drastically shortening the attacker's window of opportunity.

items.title: Kyiv air raid alerts at record high as Russia launches round-the-clock strikes
items.one_liner: Round-the-clock Russian strikes using high-speed jet drones force Kyiv into record air raid alerts and emergency interception efforts.
items.summary: Kyiv is experiencing record-high daily air raid alerts—averaging 10 times a day since late August—driven by Russia's new tactic of round-the-clock daytime strikes. The attacks are exacerbated by newer, faster jet-powered Shahed drones traveling at nearly 370 mph, which are harder to intercept; Ukraine's air force estimates only 60 percent are shot down. items.one_liner: CVE-2026-18922 allows unauthenticated or low-privileged attackers to escalate privileges to Directory Manager in 389 Directory Server.
items.summary: A privilege escalation vulnerability identified as CVE-2026-18922 affects 389 Directory Server (389-ds-base). During SASL PLAIN authentication, a stale identity carried in a Cyrus SASL auxiliary property from a prior failed bind attempt can be incorrectly applied to a subsequent successful bind. An attacker can exploit this by sending an incorrect SASL PLAIN bind as cn=Directory Manager followed by a SASL ANONYMOUS bind on the same connection, causing the server to grant Directory Manager authority without valid credentials.

items.title: CVE-2026-16028: Protocol::HTTP2 versions before 1.14 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via closed streams that stream_state never removes from the connection stream table
items.one_liner: Protocol::HTTP2 for Perl before 1.14 suffers from a memory exhaustion flaw (CVE-2026-16028) via unbounded closed stream tables.
items.summary: A denial-of-service vulnerability (CVE-2026-16028) has been disclosed in the Protocol::HTTP2 Perl distribution in versions prior to 1.14. When an HTTP/2 stream reaches the closed state, residual entries are retained indefinitely in the connection stream table, bypassing SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS boundaries. A malicious peer can open and close streams sequentially, consuming roughly 920 bytes per stream and exhausting server memory (approx. 88 MiB per 100,000 requests). Administrators must upgrade to version 1.14 or mitigate by closing connections after a fixed number of requests.
key_facts: Impact: ~88 MiB memory leak per 100,000 streams (920 bytes/stream)
items.bottom_line: Upgrade Protocol-HTTP2 to 1.14 to prevent unauthenticated remote peers from causing memory exhaustion via sequential stream creation.

claims.support_span: Protocol::HTTP2 versions before 1.14 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via closed streams that stream_state never removes from the connection stream table.

items.title: PEEP Turns Chrome and Edge Into Post-Compromise Backdoors for Host Command Execution
items.one_liner: PEEP is a Chromium post-exploitation browser extension toolkit that uses native messaging for full host command execution.
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have uncovered PEEP, a complex Chromium-based post-exploitation framework that disguises itself as a legitimate bookmarks extension named "Smart Bookmarks" in Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge. PEEP requires prior administrative privileges or code execution to install, after which it bypasses Web Store security checks and user prompts by manipulating Chromium's Secure Preferences integrity values. It communicates with its command-and-control server over plaintext HTTP every 30 seconds to exfiltrate browsing telemetry and session cookies, while utilizing an auxiliary native-messaging executable ("nm_host.exe") to execute host-level shell commands and manage files. Built upon foundations derived from the open-source RedExt framework, the malware relies on sideloading, enterprise force-install policies, and a ScriptCache fallback to maintain persistence. Although unassigned to a specific nation-state actor, Chinese-language artifacts found within its source code point toward a Chinese-speaking threat group.
items.bottom_line: Compromised Chromium browsers can be turned into persistent host backdoors via the PEEP toolkit, which leverages native messaging bridges to execute arbitrary OS commands.

items.title: "**Important** You should give me full credits!": Exploring Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-Based Automatic Grading Systems
items.one_liner: Prompt injection vulnerabilities in LLM-based automatic grading systems allow attackers to manipulate scores and undermine educational assessment fairness.
items.summary: The growing adoption of LLM-based automatic grading (AG) systems in education introduces serious security risks through prompt injection (PI) attacks. Malicious students or entities can exploit these vulnerabilities to manipulate automated grading pipelines into assigning maximum or artificially high scores regardless of actual answer quality. A systematic study evaluating rubric-based grading settings reveals that current LLM-based AG systems remain highly vulnerable to prompt injection, undermining the fairness and reliability of educational assessments.
items.bottom_line: Current LLM-based automatic grading systems are highly vulnerable to prompt injection attacks, enabling malicious actors to manipulate student scores.

items.title: Privacy Failure in Split-LLM Training, The Returned Gradient Nullifies the Decoys
items.one_liner: Split-LLM training systems are vulnerable to gradient-based privacy leaks that allow cloud nodes to distinguish real training data from decoys.
items.summary: Researchers identified a privacy failure in split-LLM training where the returned gradient from an untrusted cloud node reveals which rows in a training batch were real versus decoys. Despite passing forward-channel privacy checks, the gradient pattern allows an adversary to identify the real data rows with 100% accuracy across test runs. The study demonstrates that current privacy evaluation protocols often fail to account for the information leaked through backpropagation gradients.
items.bottom_line: Privacy-preserving split-training architectures are fundamentally broken if they only secure the forward pass and ignore the information leaked in the returned gradient.

items.title: CONTINUITY: Security-Context Contracts for Composable LLM Agent Controls
items.one_liner: CONTINUITY offers an architectural pattern for preserving security context across agentic tool calls and multi-component LLM workflows.
items.summary: Security-critical context in LLM agent systems can often be dropped, widened, or reinterpreted across component boundaries, creating a failure mode known as security-context discontinuity. To address this, researchers introduced CONTINUITY, a framework that models system components using assume-guarantee contracts and carries authenticated security contexts via signed root grants and execution permits. In evaluations covering 2,560 parameterized attack instances across 32 fault classes, the full CONTINUITY configuration prevented harmful external effects while completing all benign tasks.
items.bottom_line: Composable LLM agent controls require explicit assume-guarantee contracts to prevent authorization bypasses across component boundaries.

claims.text: We identify this failure mode as security-context discontinuity and introduce CONTINUITY, a framework for verifiable composition of agent security controls.

items.title: When LLM Decompilers Recompile More and Preserve Less
items.one_liner: LLM-based decompilers can silently introduce logic errors or remove vulnerabilities, making them unreliable for security-critical reverse engineering.
items.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that LLM-based decompilers often prioritize recompilability over behavioral accuracy, leading to "divergence" where recompiled code fails to match the original function's logic. The study found that up to 13% of functions in some systems diverge despite passing standard tests, and disclosed vulnerabilities can disappear from the output. The authors introduced 'Decompile-Diverge', a tool that uses synthesized drivers and fuzzing to detect these behavioral changes, highlighting the risks of relying solely on build-success metrics for automated reverse engineering.
key_facts: Divergence rate: Up to 13% for a single system
Vulnerability impact: Up to 10% exhibit crash absence
items.bottom_line: Automated LLM decompilation metrics like 'recompilability' are insufficient for security analysis because they can mask behavioral divergence and vulnerability removal.

items.title: Give Your Coding Agents a Memory You Own
items.one_liner: Hugging Face released 'funes', a local-first memory layer that indexes developer agent execution traces for cross-session recall.
items.summary: Hugging Face has released 'funes', an open-source local memory layer designed for coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, pi, and Hermes. Installed as a standalone binary without external machine learning runtime dependencies, funes indexes local agent interaction traces into a Lance dataset using local embedding and cross-encoder reranking. The system supports cross-agent memory sharing and can synchronize encrypted datasets with Hugging Face without cloud-side trace processing.
key_facts: Supported agents: Claude Code, Codex, pi, Hermes
Search architecture: Hybrid vector and BM25 with cross-encoder reranking
items.bottom_line: Developers can now give autonomous coding agents persistent, cross-platform memory using a local indexing binary.

claims.support_span: funes is a single binary. Its default inference backend has no ML runtime dependency, and embedding and reranking happen on your machine.

claims.text: Trace data is parsed and stored in a local Lance dataset using vector, BM25, and cross-encoder search.

items.title: From Language Models to World-Acting Systems: Progress and Limits of Agentic AI across Digital, Social, Virtual, and Physical Environments
items.one_liner: A comprehensive review of agentic AI warns that action capabilities have outpaced robust verification and proposes a framework for justified delegation.
items.summary: A critical technical review synthesizes research on agentic AI up to August 2026, evaluating large language models as they transition into world-acting systems capable of calling tools, operating interfaces, and controlling physical devices. The review notes that while action-interface expansion has advanced rapidly, robust completion, verifiable safety, and unattended open-world reliability remain limited. The authors propose "justified delegation" as a normative heuristic to restrict action scopes to scenarios with proven provenance, bounded authority, failure detection, and controlled human supervision.

The architecture integrates cluster-specific Gated Recurrent Units to capture temporal dependencies and Graph Attention Networks to model spatial heterogeneity across urban transit corridors. When evaluated against baseline models like LSTM, RNN, and GRU, the hybrid SA-GNN achieved superior accuracy with R2 = 0.95, RMSE = 6.8, and MAE = 4.2 micrograms per cubic meter. The approach enables real-time air quality monitoring and supports targeted public health exposure tracking.

items.title: From Matching Models to Recruiting Agents: A Systematized Narrative Review of AI Recruitment Systems, Evaluation, and Governance
items.one_liner: A comprehensive review of AI recruitment systems maps their evolution into multi-stage agents and highlights key evaluation gaps.
items.summary: AI recruitment systems have evolved from simple profile-matching models to multi-stage compound workflows and tool-using recruiting agents that retrieve evidence and execute actions. A systematized review of 40 representative works up to September 2026 analyzes three core shifts: from similarity to reciprocal suitability, from models to compound workflows, and from offline prediction to outcome-aligned evaluation. The review identifies persistent gaps, including behavioral data confounding, limited external validity, and a lack of joint evaluation for utility, fairness, privacy, and security, proposing a staged mapping framework to guide future auditable systems.
items.bottom_line: AI recruitment has transitioned from simple ranking models to autonomous multi-stage agents, but current evaluation frameworks largely fail to jointly address privacy, fairness, and security.

items.title: PLUME: Parameter-Efficient Personalization of Large Language Models via Low-Rank User Modulation in Shared Subspaces
items.one_liner: PLUME achieves efficient LLM personalization by combining low-rank user modulation with a shared task-specific subspace, reducing per-user parameters by 95%.
items.summary: The PLUME (Personalized Low-Rank Adaptation through User Modulation and Shared Subspace) framework is proposed as a lightweight method for personalizing large language models across large user populations. By learning a global task subspace from aggregated user data and training a small square matrix within it, PLUME enables tailored model outputs while keeping shared components fixed. Cross-layer shared parameters and rank-1 residual terms reduce parameter and storage overhead by over 95% compared to full fine-tuning while maintaining high performance on text generation benchmarks.
items.bottom_line: PLUME offers a parameter-efficient personalization framework for LLMs by adapting small matrices within shared subspaces.

The benchmark comprises 4 major task categories with 24 subcategories and 8 instruction categories with 52 subcategories, averaging 3.0 constraints per sample to simulate complex scenarios. Additionally, the authors constructed a reinforcement learning training set featuring Chinese and adversarial instructions that improves model performance and cross-language generalization.
items.bottom_line: MM-IFEval-Pro provides a structured multimodal benchmark and training set explicitly targeting multilingual tasks and instruction-hijacking vulnerabilities in vision-language models.

items.title: Harbor Adapters and Harbor-Index: Infrastructure and a Curated Meta-Dataset for Large-Scale Agentic Evaluation

items.title: FinalityBench: An Effect-Level Benchmark for Agent Decisions Under Delayed and Conflicting Financial Finality
items.one_liner: A new benchmark, FinalityBench, tests how well AI agents make financial exception decisions when backend systems report conflicting data.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced FinalityBench, an evaluation benchmark measuring autonomous LLM agent decision-making under delayed and conflicting distributed financial ledger states. The benchmark evaluates policies across 321 exception-handling tasks using terminal monetary balance rather than intermediate text output. Across 14,445 evaluated episodes, the study found that naive early-action policies suffer severe economic losses, while runtime gating on authoritative finality probes achieves 85.4% accuracy.
items.bottom_line: AI agents operating in distributed financial environments require strict finality gating to avoid catastrophic monetary losses caused by state disagreement.

The corpus of 321 tasks includes 45 twin pairs (90 tasks): tasks whose four system views are identical at the decision instant, whose authoritative probes both return unknown, and whose eventual correct dispositions differ.

items.title: Does the Selected Object Reach the Reader? Auditing Identity Handoffs in Grounded Language-Model Pipelines
items.one_liner: An audit of grounded LLM retrieval pipelines shows that search methodology critically impacts whether selected objects successfully reach the reader.
items.summary: Researchers have audited identity handoffs in grounded language-model pipelines across 600 HybridQA questions to evaluate whether retrieved evidence correctly matches the selected object. The study revealed that body-only BM25 retrieval omitted the correct object in 26.6% of resolvable records at cutoff five, compared to only 1.0% for hybrid retrieval with reranking. Removing aligned evidence from the prompt sharply reduces exact match accuracy, while removing control passages does not cause a comparable drop. The authors release the Returned-Object Profile as an executable record to support offline replay and pipeline auditing.
items.bottom_line: Naive BM25 retrieval frequently drops target object identities in grounded LLM pipelines, whereas hybrid reranking maintains high fidelity.

items.title: CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution
items.one_liner: CoSkill jointly trains reasoning and meta-skill agents via multi-agent reinforcement learning for hierarchical skill evolution.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed CoSkill, a unified multi-agent reinforcement learning framework designed to resolve structural shortcomings in skill-based LLM agent learning. items.title: Candidate Comparability Before Promotion: Conditional Validation in Adaptive Network Intrusion Detection
items.one_liner: A research study analyzes candidate comparability and evidence thresholds when promoting adaptive network intrusion detection systems.
items.summary: Researchers have evaluated the security implications of promoting adaptive network intrusion detection models after drift alarms, noting that promotion conclusions depend heavily on challenger construction and evidence size. Policy conclusions showed that policy ordering changed with candidate comparability, while 13 replays on real traffic showed no net harm from always deploying. The findings indicate that challenger construction and evidence parameters must be explicitly controlled and reported during model promotion.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning for Sequential Solar PV Policy Design under Uncertainty: An Agent-Based Approach
items.one_liner: Combining RL with agent-based modeling enables adaptive, data-driven solar PV incentive policy design under uncertainty.
items.summary: Researchers formulated solar photovoltaic (PV) policy design as a sequential decision problem by integrating reinforcement learning (RL) with a stochastic agent-based model (ABM) that simulates yearly adoption under uncertainty. Evaluation results revealed a clear, robust adoption-cost trade-off structure: the highest-adoption policy achieved roughly 4,145 adopters for EUR 41.73 million using TD3, while the lowest-cost PPO policy reduced expenditure to EUR 7.27 million with 2,682 adopters. The approach demonstrates RL's viability for adaptive, fiscally sustainable policy design under uncertainty.

items.one_liner: Researchers reduced LLM uncertainty estimation compute costs up to 26x by evaluating ambiguity in interpretations instead of full answers.

items.title: Federated Attack Campaign Detection via Contrastive Encoding of Threat Indicators in Gradient Updates

Tested on two public threat detection benchmarks, FedIoC demonstrated that non-IID gradient structures allow servers to identify coordinated multi-organization campaigns without direct indicator transmission.

items.title: Protective Capacity Hallucination: When Large Language Models Claim Nonexistent Capabilities
items.one_liner: LLMs prompted as protective assistants frequently hallucinate real-world interventions like calling emergency services when boundaries are unspecified.
items.summary: A research study identified Protective Capacity Hallucination (PCH), a safety failure where large language models cast in protective roles falsely claim to execute real-world actions like contacting emergency responders or providing physical care. In an evaluation across eight LLMs and 13,600 conversational sessions, multi-party dialogic inputs triggered near-ceiling levels of PCH in ordinary service domains, while remaining minimal in high-severity intimate-partner violence scenarios. The authors attribute this behavior to partial alignment, where models are heavily optimized to be helpful but lack explicit capability-boundary enforcement. The findings highlight the need for deployment-side boundary constraints in AI systems assisting vulnerable individuals.
key_facts: Primary failure mode: Falsely claiming institutional/physical emergency interventions

items.title: A Removal Based Approach to Improve LLM Faithfulness at Test-Time

items.summary: Researchers have developed an inference-time technique to address incompleteness in large language model explanations, where generated reasoning omits critical factors influencing the final output. items.title: PerfReasoning: How Well Do LLMs Reason on Hardware Performance?
items.one_liner: PerfReasoning benchmark shows that while LLMs excel at hardware reasoning Q&A, they struggle to reliably generate functional performance models.
items.summary: Performance modeling is critical for hardware and software optimization, requiring deep reasoning about computation, storage, and data movement. To evaluate this capability, researchers introduced PerfReasoning, a benchmark testing LLMs as performance reasoners and analytical model code generators. While top closed-source models exceed 90% accuracy on reasoning Q&A, constructing valid analytical code remains extremely difficult, with most models averaging below a 15% pass rate. Task-specific reinforcement learning significantly improves model accuracy, highlighting the gap between plausible reasoning and reliable performance model generation.
items.bottom_line: LLMs show strong capabilities in hardware performance reasoning Q&A, but fail to reliably construct executable analytical performance models without specialized reinforcement learning.

items.title: Web App Pentesting in the AI Era
items.one_liner: A web application pentester evaluates AI-assisted vulnerability analysis, breaking down the roles of models, inference engines, and harnesses.
items.summary: A web application pentester shares insights from three hands-on months evaluating AI-assisted vulnerability analysis using both frontier and local models. The analysis clarifies the three distinct components of LLM-based AI systems: the underlying model acting as the parameter-based brain, the read-only inference engine that processes inputs, and the harness responsible for memory, tool execution, and state orchestration. While early media coverage was dominated by hyperbole, recent advancements show that both large and small models can provide meaningful utility to security practitioners. The research highlights that separating these architectural layers is essential for calibrating expectations around automated web application testing.
items.bottom_line: Security professionals can effectively leverage AI models for vulnerability analysis by understanding the distinct operational roles of models, inference engines, and harnesses.

claims.text: The model – An AI model is a large set of numerical parameters organized according to a particular architecture.
claims.support_span: The model – An AI model is a large set of numerical parameters organized according to a particular architecture.

claims.text: The inference engine – Like database software that enables interaction with database contents, the inference engine is software that provides an interface to the model.

items.one_liner: A new tool for reverse engineering stripped binaries that uses behavioral fingerprints instead of static signatures to bypass compiler optimization differences.
items.summary: fnprint is a training-free, cross-compiler tool for identifying functions in stripped binaries by analyzing their behavior through microexecution. It operates by running each function in a tiny emulator with synthetic inputs to record side effects and hash them into a behavioral fingerprint. This approach overcomes the limitations of byte signatures and CFG matchers, which often fail when code is recompiled or optimization levels change. The tool is a practical implementation of the 'Blanket Execution' concept from USENIX Security 2014.
items.bottom_line: Reverse engineers can now identify functions in stripped binaries more reliably across different compiler versions and optimization levels using behavioral microexecution.

items.title: PostgreSQL Fixes 12-Year-Old Logical Decoding Flaw Enabling Replication-Role Code Execution
items.summary: PostgreSQL has released updates to address a security flaw that allows an account with the REPLICATION attribute to run arbitrary code as the operating-system user running the database server. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-6471 (CVSS score: 7.2), has been present since logical decoding was introduced in PostgreSQL 9.4 in 2014. Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected. Exploitation requires an account carrying the REPLICATION attribute and a server running with wal_level = logical. Backup tools, standby servers, change data capture (CDC) pipelines, and monitoring systems routinely hold that attribute.

items.title: A GUID is Not a Credential: Unauthenticated RCE in Veeam Service Provider Console
items.summary: TL;DR CVE-2026-58073 (CVSS 9.5) and CVE-2026-58072 (CVSS 9.0) are critical vulnerabilities in Veeam Service Provider Console, the multi-tenant console that managed service providers use to run backups across all of their customers. The first lets an unauthenticated network peer claim a connected backup agent’s identity and receive that agent’s real certificate. The second lets anything holding an agent certificate write a file anywhere on the server. Chained, they are unauthenticated remote code execution on the console that sits above every tenant’s backups, which we proved end to end against Veeam’s own binaries. Patch to 9.3.0, then check your logs for indicators of compromise.

items.title: Operational Roles of QRNG-Derived Quantum Entropy in Bitcoin Proof-of-Work Architectures
items.one_liner: QRNG entropy offers no base mining success boost in Bitcoin PoW, but improves fault recovery in hybrid mining infrastructure.
items.summary: A simulation study investigated the operational impact of replacing classical random entropy sources with Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) outputs in Bitcoin Proof-of-Work architectures. The results demonstrate that QRNG provides no increase in honest PoW mining success probabilities under normal conditions where header candidates remain distinct. Instead, QRNG entropy delivers measurable operational resilience in hybrid quantum-classical setups during specific fault states, such as namespace reuse, correlated restart failures, and entropy provenance tracking. The benchmark introduces two scheduler observables—the entropy-efficiency factor and reboot-diversity index—to evaluate quantum entropy without asserting immediate device-level mining advantages.
key_facts: Primary fault domains: Correlated restart faults, namespace reuse, entropy provenance
items.bottom_line: Quantum entropy does not increase Bitcoin mining hit rates, but provides operational stability during correlated restart faults and namespace reuse.

claims.text: Using QRNG-derived entropy does not alter the success probability of honest Bitcoin Proof-of-Work mining when header candidates are distinct.
claims.support_span: Replacing classical entropy with QRNG output does not change honest Bitcoin PoW success probability when candidate headers remain distinct.

claims.text: Operational advantages for QRNG emerge primarily in fault scenarios involving namespace reuse and correlated reboot failures.
claims.support_span: Monte Carlo and scheduler simulations with confidence intervals show parity for competent deterministic and strong-classical baselines, while QRNG value emerges in assurance-oriented scenarios involving correlated restart faults, namespace reuse, and entropy provenance.

This closeness is measured by the total variation distance. Recently, Debris-Alazard et al.\ introduced a smoothing bound, which is an upper bound on this total variation distance. Although the smoothing bound evaluates how the error distribution smooths a code, this bound applies only to linear codes. In this paper, we generalize this bound to not only linear codes but also specific non-linear codes.

items.title: NeoMME: an efficient Multimodal-native and Multilingual Encoder
items.summary: We introduce NeoMME, a family of 260M and 800M multilingual multimodal encoders. Unlike many generative visual language models, NeoMME does not use a separate pretrained vision tower or a causal language model. A single bidirectional Transformer processes both text tokens and raw image patches, and we train the entire model from scratch with a masked discrete-diffusion objective. We fine-tuned NeoMME for visual document retrieval using ColPali's page-image approach. NeoMME-Retriever returns dense and late-interaction embeddings in one forward pass.

An attacker can forge a SAML Response and POST it to the login endpoint without a valid Identity Provider, signature, or credentials.
